cues.text: Two sisters, a new town
Ada Hegerberg was born in 1995 in Molde, in Norway, and grew up in Sunndalsøra.
She played football there with her older sister, Andrine.
In 2007 the family moved to a new town, Kolbotn.
Lift the flap to see who came along.
Andrine joined the new club, Kolbotn, with her.
In 2011, at sixteen, Ada became the youngest player ever to score a hat-trick in Norway’s top women’s league.
Moving somewhere new is hard. Family by your side can make it easier.
Far from home
In 2013 the sisters moved to Germany, to play for Turbine Potsdam.
That summer, Ada played for Norway in the European Championship final, and Norway lost 1–0 to Germany.
Her club also finished second in the league and the cup.
Open the door to France.
In 2014, Ada moved on to Lyon, in France.
In her first season there, she scored 26 goals in 22 league games.
Coming second can hurt. It’s okay to feel disappointed, and then keep going.
Speaking up
Ada disagreed with Norway’s football association about how it treated women’s football.
In 2017, she decided to stop playing for the national team, as a protest.
Some things got better, but she felt there was still a long way to go.
Flip the sign.
Standing up cost her something: she missed the 2019 World Cup.
She later said her time with the national team had left her feeling very low.
Speaking up for what is fair takes courage, even when it costs you something.
A message for girls
In 2018, Ada became the very first winner of the women’s Ballon d’Or.
She called the new award a huge step forward.
Raise the golden ball.
That night, she had a message for young girls around the world: believe in yourselves.
She also said she knew how important it is to have role models to look up to.
In 2019, she scored three goals in just 16 minutes as Lyon won the Champions League final.
Believe in yourself, and remember that someone younger may be looking up to you.
Twenty-one months
In January 2020, Ada badly hurt her knee.
A scan showed that she had torn an important ligament, called the ACL.
She would be out for a very long time.
Flip the calendar pages.
It took 21 months before she played for Lyon again, in October 2021.
A month later she scored twice against Paris Saint-Germain, and in 2022 she scored in the Champions League final as Lyon won again.
Healing takes time. Be patient with yourself, and count the small steps.
Back for Norway
Norway’s football association got a new president, Lise Klaveness.
Ada talked with her in depth about the future of women’s football.
In March 2022, Ada decided to come back to the national team after five years away.
Open the gate.
In her first game back, on 7 April 2022, Ada scored three goals as Norway beat Kosovo 5–1.
She had stood up for fairness, and now she was back in Norway’s shirt.
Standing up for what’s right can change things. When things get fairer, you can come back stronger.
